I've attached a redacted sample invoice (sample-invoice.csv) that shows how we currently map invoice lines; can you show how Redwood would map the same traffic? Also cc'ing Sonia from our platform team — she may want a quick math walk-through.

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear asks and the sample invoice. Quick summary up-front, then a worked example attached.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Minimum billing quantum: Redwood charges per token unit with a minimum slab of 256 token-units per request-window for streaming calls; long conversation history is amortized across conversation windows rather than billed in full on every turn.
- KV-cache / heartbeat credits: We apply a one-time "prefix warmup" credit when a conversation rehydrates a cached KV for an active session; credits show as negative invoice lines tied to the conversation ID.
- Pilot discounts: yes, pilot discount arithmetic is applied after adding/subtracting credits (i.e., credits reduce the billable base before discount).

Attached is a short PDF (metering-examples.pdf) with a side-by-side of your sample-invoice mapped to Redwood's model. Below is a concise worked example so you can see the math inline.

Worked example (short):
- Scenario: conversation with 45k tokens of retained history, user sends a 120-token prompt, model responds 230 tokens.
- Our session window grouping: we consider the active request + cached KV references, and we bill the active call against the 256 token-unit minimum per request-window. The 45k retained history is only *counted* when it is material to the new token generation (e.g., if we need to re-infer embeddings or expand beyond cached keys); typical reuse via KV cache avoids re-billing the full history each turn.
- Example math: request tokens billed = max(120 + 230, 256) = 350 tokens billed for that request-window. If the preceding turn warmed the KV and triggered a "heartbeat" (a short prefix load), we credit a one-time -128 token-unit warmup credit on the invoice line for that conversation.

Notes/operational details:
- Rounding: final token units are floored to the nearest whole token, and invoice lines are aggregated daily per conversation id. Small per-request fractionation is not charged; we round up only at the quantum boundary.
- Exceptions: extremely long full-history re-materialization (e.g., forced full-context recall >100k tokens) is charged as a special ingestion line; we'll surface that during onboarding.

Next steps: Jonas (cc'd) can run a short mapping of your sample-invoice rows to Redwood's invoice line model; Vanessa will add a recommended pilot concession (if you move to a 3-month pilot, we can provide a capped warmup credit). I'm free for a quick 30-min call tomorrow if Sonia wants to walk through the spreadsheet.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt

Hi Sonia / Michael — quick answers and proposed MA (mutual action):

Answers: 
1) Conversation id definition: we treat your application-level conversation id as the primary key. If you shard per-tab, you can map all shards to the same canonical conversation id during ingestion; otherwise we'll treat each shard as a separate conversation for KV purposes.
2) Warmup credit scope: applied per conversation id rehydrate event (not per VM). If you have ephemeral shards mapped to one canonical id, you'll receive one warmup credit when the canonical KV is first rehydrated.
3) Dedicated pool during pilot: warmup credits still apply because credits are usage-accounting artifacts, even if compute is reserved. However, for dedicated pilots we typically combine warmup credits into a single onboarding credit (so you don't accumulate many small negative lines).

Proposed mutual action plan (MA):
- Today: Redwood will map your sample-invoice to our invoice model (Jonas to deliver by EOD Tuesday).
- Tue: Quick sync (30 min) to walk the mapped rows with Sonia + Procurement.
- If Orchard signs pilot (3 months, Dedicated pool): Redwood issues a one-time onboarding credit of 250k token-units AND applies the standard pilot percentage discount (15%) to billable usage. Credits are applied before discounting.

I'll add these MA items to the HubSpot deal and send a short one-pager summarizing the concession math. Vanessa, can you confirm the final concession language?

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
